title: Why Social Media Brands Are Moving Toward More Human Content
tldr: Argues brands are shifting from polished to human-centered, authentic content on social — a direct signal of where audiences and platforms are heading. Aligns with the people-over-polish trend.
angle: Why 'good enough and human' now outperforms polished brand content — and how to operationalize it.

title: Trust Is the Business Model: What 15 Years of Her Canberra Teaches Publishers About Thriving in the Age of AI
tldr: Uses a 15-year local publisher case study to argue trust is the durable moat as news trust falls to 37% globally in 2026. Concrete lessons on audience-first publishing amid AI disruption.
angle: Trust as content strategy: what a small local publisher teaches enterprise comms teams.

title: Taylor Swift's latest album announcement raises a question about audience fatigue
tldr: Uses Swift's endless variant/announcement cycle to probe when engagement tips into audience fatigue — a sharp lens on media-consumption limits.
angle: The fatigue threshold: how much content drip is too much before your audience tunes out.

title: Dentsu taps microdrama trend for Co-op
tldr: Co-op's first microdrama becomes a test case — and the piece questions whether it's a genuinely new format or a relabelling of short-form serial content. Useful format-trend skepticism.
angle: Microdrama: real format shift or rebranded short-form? A framework for judging 'new' formats.

title: The myth of the changing consumer
tldr: Argues that 'the consumer is changing' is often a lazy narrative and you should look for the context behind any trend. A corrective to trend-chasing content strategy.
angle: How to interrogate a 'consumer trend' before you build content strategy around it.

title: 'Not hiring' entry-level talent: Industry acknowledges runaway crisis brought on by introducing AI to the workforce
tldr: The ad/media industry admits AI is gutting entry-level hiring, with implications for how content and comms teams are staffed and trained. A real structural shift, not routine.
angle: If AI replaces juniors, where does the next generation of content strategists come from?

title: Joseph Clark on why he's keeping AI out of Oh Studio, and the protest film that went viral saying so
tldr: An animation director built a remote studio and a viral protest film around rejecting AI — a human-craft counter-position that resonated widely. Strong case of stance-as-brand.
angle: When 'no AI' becomes a brand: the marketing power of a human-craft stance.

title: Publishers are rebuilding for the post-search era
tldr: DPS execs describe prioritizing direct audiences, diversified revenue and AI strategies as search referral traffic collapses. Core to owned-media and audience strategy right now.
angle: Building direct audience relationships when Google referral traffic dries up.

title: I helped shape McLaren's brand. Here's what worries me about the refresh
tldr: A former head of brand argues the loud backlash to McLaren's rebrand isn't about the logo — it's about deeper narrative and meaning. Insider reputation/rebrand breakdown.
why_fresh: insider rebrand analysis but familiar rebrand-backlash genre
angle: Rebrand backlash is never about the logo: reading the narrative underneath.

title: QSR: Why McDonald's Is Becoming a Media Company
tldr: Breaks down how McDonald's is building out owned media and retail-media muscle, joining brands acting like publishers. A concrete brand-as-media case.
angle: When fast food becomes a media company: the owned-media playbook for legacy brands.

title: 'I'm a strategist.' But are you?
tldr: Challenges communicators who claim the 'strategist' label but skip research, measurement and evaluation. A pointed prompt on what strategy actually requires.
angle: What separates a real strategist from a self-declared one: the measurement test.

title: Target makes its red bag the center of Inside Out
tldr: Campaign breakdown of how Target turned its iconic red bag into a branded storytelling device tied to Inside Out. A tidy visual-storytelling case study.
angle: Turning a brand asset into a story character: the red-bag playbook.

title: Young adult content strategy pays off for Prime Video
tldr: Prime Video's deliberate YA-focused content strategy is driving results — a concrete example of audience-segment-led content bets.
angle: Betting on one audience segment: what Prime Video's YA push teaches content planners.

title: AI Isn't Disrupting the PESO Model. It's Proving It.
tldr: Dietrich reviews two new surveys ranking PESO channels for AI visibility and argues the data reinforces integrated owned/earned/paid strategy rather than upending it.
angle: AI visibility as the new proof point for integrated PESO strategy.
